etymologies.etymologyHTML: From crook, equivalent to crook +‎ -ed.

definitions.definition: simple past and past participle of crook

etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English croked, crokid, past participle of croken (“to crook, bend”). Cognate with Danish kroget (“crooked”). More at crook.

definitions.definition: Not straight; having one or more bends or angles.
Set at an angle; not vertical or square.

quote.citation: 2004, Peter Bondanella, chapter 4, in Hollywood Italians: Dagos, Palookas, Romeos, Wise Guys, and Sopranos, pages 173–174:
quote.text: During the height of Italian immigration in the United States and in New York City, gangs flourished not only because of poverty but also because of political and social corruption. Policemen and politicians were often as crooked as the gang leaders themselves.
